title: Kinetic Energy

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 11 — Work, Energy and Power

explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy an object possesses due to its motion, and it grows with the SQUARE of velocity — doubling speed quadruples kinetic energy, a frequently tested exam trap. It is always non-negative and is a scalar quantity.

workedExample.scenario: A 1000 kg car travels at 20 m/s.

commonMistakes: Forgetting the square on velocity — assuming kinetic energy scales linearly with speed rather than quadratically.
Using v as displacement or momentum by mistake in multi-step problems.
genZNote: Double the speed, QUADRUPLE the kinetic energy — physics does not do linear scaling here, and exams love testing exactly that.
